title: Todd Solondz and "Welcome To The Dollhouse" (1995)

commenti.body:
I was pleasantly surprised to see this. Like a lot of girls, I *was* Dawn Weiner. Solondz was bullied himself, and he crafted that awful feeling so well I’m getting choked up thinking about it. The double-punch of making her home life even more cruel than her school was almost too mean. Dressing Missy in her little outfit and always having her dancing in the corner, *gloating* about having all the things Dawn so desperately wants even *one* of and can’t ever have. 

Even being kidnapped, the worst thing that can happen to a child, worked out great for Missy- she didn’t even know anything bad happened. Dawn sees this and knows that someone *wanted* Missy in a way nobody could ever *want* her, and it’s true- Dawn, a minor female, wandered around New York City and nobody even noticed her. I used to to do the same thing, wander around alone daring someone to abduct me just to prove someone *noticed* me and nobody ever did. The invisibility of the ugly woman contrasted by her screaming to be seen, the foreboding tone that indicates this will be the rest of Dawn’s life.

I’d like to bring up the sequel, Weiner Dog. Spoilers 



In this movie, Dawn’s fate is retconned. During Palindromes it is revealed that Dawn went to college, gained 100 lbs, got pregnant from date rape, and committed suicide upon finding out. In Weinerdog, Dawn is alive and well, re-cast as Greta Gerwig, working with animals and having set boundaries with her awful family. Brandon Sexton Junior’s character comes across her, apologizes, and they get together.

I submit that this was not Dawn’s real ending. Instead, it was her pre-suicide fantasy, probably one she’d had for a long time. As an ugly woman, when I fantasize about good things happening to me, I envision Pretty Me; the woman I wish I looked like, the version of me I *imagine* is being mooed at or having shit thrown at me from cars. I think Dawn retreated into this fantasy as she died, and her walking into the sunset with BSJ’s character and her dog was her finally taking control over her life as she died.

I cannot think of another reason he would give Dawn Weiner a good ending, but not cast Heather Matarazzo to play her.

> I used to to do the same thing, wander around alone daring someone to abduct me just to prove someone noticed me

Holy shit. I'm so sorry you ever had those feelings.

I lost weight and fixed my teeth, so I’m mostly fine now. The worst thing about being an ugly woman is that we start being sexualized when we are like 11, so by the time we are 12 we know if we are an unfuckable sow or a beautiful princess. Having to live with that as a child, a couple years after we stop being scared of the dark, is a huge mindfuck. When Dawn would do *anything* to get violated by that greasy loser teenager guy, it’s not so much because she felt desire for him but because of the validation he represents. Same as her waiting around school to “get raped” by Brandon Sexton, Jr. Even if it’s couched in horrible violence, Dawn is so love- and probably touch-starved already (her parents don’t hug her once) she would *wait around* for that kind of attention, willing to put up with abuse couched as love. Versus Missy got that (what Dawn sees as) external validation without even trying, and she didn’t even have to experience pain or fear, having thought it was a game.

this is what makes the movie so painful to watch but so also important - it's such a deep dive into young girls who are rarely seen so clearly and with such compassion. I don't think the point was for people to watch and think she deserved to be bullied, just the opposite - why is being something other than a living doll like her sister a reason for anyone to pick on Dawn? she's a little kid starting to have adult feelings in an environment that judges her so harshly for really stupid reasons (primarily how she looks). kids are awkward - they're still figuring everything out. 

I had a similar realization at 10 - why was Jenny treated differently by adults and the boys? oh - she's considered pretty. I don't get treated like that so I guess I'm not. sexualizing children is so fucked up and people do it so mindlessly, oblivious to the fact that girls understand what's happening and internalize it deeply.

I really like the Todd Solondz films I've seen, Welcome To The Doll House, Happiness, and its sequel Life During Wartime. 

His films are for those that like black humor, laughing and sympathizing with those who are the most ostracized by society. Pedophiles are characters in a lot of his movies. 

Welcome To The Dollhouse definitely captures the late 80s and 90s amazingly well. The way the characters talk is how teenagers talked then.

I admire the choice not to give Dawn any special talents or exceptional qualities. She was just an ordinary adolescent girl, who is exactly as selfish and animalistic as we all were at that age. So often they make the ugly girls extra smart or athletic or at least nice. Dawn, clearly, would have been one of her own bullies if she’d been born a little prettier. 

I mean, look at her family. She had no chance to learn compassion or kindness for kindness’s sake. Her parents were phenomenally selfish, and only doted on her brother because he could earn them bragging rights if he got into an Ivy League school later. Mark was just as unattractive as Dawn, but because he wasn’t born owing the world prettiness, he was spared the truly traumatic experience of Dawn- bullying that will shape her brain chemistry and I argue, cause CPTSD- an able to duck under the radar enough to concentrate on school. Dawn is in survival mode. Even her extracurricular singing activity which she’s supposed to enjoy, she gets bullied into dreading. How can a girl living a life like spare the brain power or find refuge enough to develop any skills? 

This
Movie does a good job showing how the really evil kids victimizing Dawn are victimized themselves. Look at the truly monstrous creature Lolita, Dawn’s classmate at school who demands Dawn have a bowel movement while she listens. What had to happen to Lolita to teach her to do this to other children? I don’t think Solondz named her Lolita for no reason at all. The female bully who bragged about being “finger-fucked” by an 18
Year old boy- when she was *eleven*- is another victim, acting out her pain by making it a social signifier. The parents by contrast have no such context presented they are just evil. Representing how godlike adults are when you are a kid.


I’m

I'm a lot like Dawn even into adulthood. It cuts close to the bone. If my life was made into a movie Todd Solondz would be the perfect director, unfortunately. But I'm trying to be less dysfunctional. Happiness is my favorite. It's up there with Melancholia when it comes to great ensemble films about how we're really all the same. I feel that life really is just a series of vignettes. It's kind of like the character in Melancholia who said life isn't too short... It's f***ing long.
Also he apparently asked Matarazzo to come back to play her, but she refused (which I understand).

There have been depictions of suburbia as quirky, melancholic yet beautiful, but *Dollhouse* is a specific kind of dull pain that showcases a bleak outlook despite people owning homes, getting to school fine and having neighbors. Dawn never rises above to be the bigger person, which is both relateable and not the happy ending we hope for.

This is one of the most honest portrayals of pre-teen life in the 90s than any film I've seen, its observations are ripped straight out of the real world. I've seen so many variations of the Dawn Wiener character and especially Brendan, the totally unpredictable young asshole bully. 

One character I found was very unique was the older brother played by the late Matthew farber. He was a nerd/outcast but totally self assured and undettered by social pressures. Nerds in films are usually shown as wanting to belong to some sort of in group or as having some sort of "deficiency" that needs to be corrected through the intervention of a contrived carefree character. Reminds me of Devo.

Heather Mattarazzo was so just amazing in her role.

All in all, great film, sadly overlooked. Todd solondz doesn't get enough credit as a truly american auteur.
